11 // Stream fork: Connects the input stream (ready-valid) handshake to *all* of `N_OUP` output stream
12 // handshakes. For each input stream handshake, every output stream handshakes exactly once. The
13 // input stream only handshakes when all output streams have handshaked, but the output streams do
14 // not have to handshake simultaneously.
15 //
16 // This module has no data ports because stream data does not need to be forked: the data of the
17 // input stream can just be applied at all output streams.
18 
19 module stream_fork #(
20     parameter int unsigned N_OUP = 0    // Synopsys DC requires a default value for parameters.
21 ) (
22     input  logic                clk_i,
23     input  logic                rst_ni,
24     input  logic                valid_i,
25     output logic                ready_o,
26     output logic [N_OUP-1:0]    valid_o,
27     input  logic [N_OUP-1:0]    ready_i
28 );
29 
30     typedef enum logic {READY, WAIT} state_t;
31 
32     logic [N_OUP-1:0]   oup_ready,
33                         all_ones;
34 
35     state_t inp_state_d, inp_state_q;
36 
37     // Input control FSM
38     always_comb begin
39         // ready_o     = 1'b0;
40         inp_state_d = inp_state_q;
41 
42         unique case (inp_state_q)
43             READY: begin
44                 if (valid_i) begin
45                     if (valid_o == all_ones && ready_i == all_ones) begin
46                         // If handshake on all outputs, handshake on input.
47                         ready_o = 1'b1;
48                     end else begin
49                         ready_o = 1'b0;
50                         // Otherwise, wait for inputs that did not handshake yet.
51                         inp_state_d = WAIT;
52                     end
53                 end else begin
54                     ready_o = 1'b0;
55                 end
56             end
57             WAIT: begin
58                 if (valid_i && oup_ready == all_ones) begin
59                     ready_o = 1'b1;
60                     inp_state_d = READY;
61                 end else begin
62                     ready_o = 1'b0;
63                 end
64             end
65             default: begin
66                 inp_state_d = READY;
67                 ready_o = 1'b0;
68             end
69         endcase
70     end
71 
72     always_ff @(posedge clk_i, negedge rst_ni) begin
73         if (!rst_ni) begin
74             inp_state_q <= READY;
75         end else begin
76             inp_state_q <= inp_state_d;
77         end
78     end
79 
80     // Output control FSM
81     for (genvar i = 0; i < N_OUP; i++) begin: gen_oup_state
82         state_t oup_state_d, oup_state_q;
83 
84         always_comb begin
85             oup_ready[i]    = 1'b1;
86             valid_o[i]      = 1'b0;
87             oup_state_d     = oup_state_q;
88 
89             unique case (oup_state_q)
90                 READY: begin
91                     if (valid_i) begin
92                         valid_o[i] = 1'b1;
93                         if (ready_i[i]) begin   // Output handshake
94                             if (!ready_o) begin     // No input handshake yet
95                                 oup_state_d = WAIT;
96                             end
97                         end else begin          // No output handshake
98                             oup_ready[i] = 1'b0;
99                         end
100                     end
101                 end
102                 WAIT: begin
103                     if (valid_i && ready_o) begin   // Input handshake
104                         oup_state_d = READY;
105                     end
106                 end
107                 default: begin
108                     oup_state_d = READY;
109                 end
110             endcase
111         end
112 
113         always_ff @(posedge clk_i, negedge rst_ni) begin
114             if (!rst_ni) begin
115                 oup_state_q <= READY;
116             end else begin
117                 oup_state_q <= oup_state_d;
118             end
119         end
120     end
121 
122     assign all_ones = '1;   // Synthesis fix for Vivado, which does not correctly compute the width
123                             // of the '1 literal when assigned to a port of parametrized width.
124 
125 // pragma translate_off
126 `ifndef VERILATOR
127     initial begin: p_assertions
128         assert (N_OUP >= 1) else $fatal(1, "Number of outputs must be at least 1!");
129     end
130 `endif
131 // pragma translate_on

6 
7 Maintainer: Nils Wistoff <nwistoff@iis.ee.ethz.ch>

125 ## Header Contents

129 ### RTL Register Macros
130 
131 The header file `registers.svh` contains macros that expand to descriptions of registers.
132 To avoid misuse of `always_ff` blocks, only the following macros shall be used to describe sequential behavior.
133 The use of linter rules that flag explicit uses of `always_ff` in source code is encouraged.
134 
135 |    Macro     |                             Arguments                             |                                Description                                |
136 | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
137 | `` `FF``     | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, (`clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`)             | Flip-flop with asynchronous active-low reset                              |
138 | `` `FFAR``   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arst_sig`                | Flip-flop with asynchronous active-high reset                             |
139 | `` `FFARN``  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`               | *deprecated* Flip-flop with asynchronous active-low reset                 |
140 | `` `FFSR``   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rst_sig`                 | Flip-flop with synchronous active-high reset                              |
141 | `` `FFSRN``  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rstn_sig`                | Flip-flop with synchronous active-low reset                               |
142 | `` `FFNR``   | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `clk_sig`                                       | Flip-flop without reset                                                   |
143 |              |                                                                   |                                                                           |
144 | `` `FFL``    | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, (`clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`) | Flip-flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset              |
145 | `` `FFLAR``  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arst_sig`    | Flip-flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-high reset             |
146 | `` `FFLARN`` | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `arstn_sig`   | *deprecated* Flip-flop with load-enable and asynchronous active-low reset |
147 | `` `FFLSR``  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rst_sig`     | Flip-flop with load-enable and synchronous active-high reset              |
148 | `` `FFLSRN`` | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `rst_val`, `clk_sig`, `rstn_sig`    | Flip-flop with load-enable and synchronous active-low reset               |
149 | `` `FFLNR``  | `q_sig`, `d_sig`, `load_ena`, `clk_sig`                           | Flip-flop with load-enable without reset                                  |
150 - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*
151 - *Argument suffix `_sig` indicates signal names for present and next state as well as clocks and resets.*
152 - *Argument `rst_val` specifies the value literal to be assigned upon reset.*
153 - *Argument `load_ena` specifies the boolean expression that forms the load enable of the register.*

155 ### SystemVerilog Assertion Macros
156 
157 The header file `assertions.svh` contains macros that expand to assertion blocks.
158 These macros should recduce the effort in writing many assertions and make it
159 easier to use them. They are identical with the macros used by [lowrisc](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_assert.sv)
160 and just re-implemented here for the sake of easier use in PULP projects (the same include guard is used so they should not clash).
161 
162 #### Simple Assertion and Cover Macros
163 | Macro                                                       | Arguments                                                                  | Description |
164 | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
165 | `` `ASSERT_I``     | `__name`, `__prop`                     | Immediate assertion                                                        |
166 | `` `ASSERT_INIT``  | `__name`, `__prop`                     | Assertion in initial block. Can be used for things like parameter checking |
167 | `` `ASSERT_FINAL`` | `__name`, `__prop`                     | Assertion in final block                                                   |
168 | `` `ASSERT``       | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`) | Assert a concurrent property directly                                      |
169 | `` `ASSERT_NEVER`` | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`) | Assert a concurrent property NEVER happens                                 |
170 | `` `ASSERT_KNOWN`` | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`)  | Concurrent clocked assertion with custom error message                     |
171 | `` `COVER``        | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`) | Cover a concurrent property                                                |
172 - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*
173 
174 #### Complex Assertion Macros
175 | Macro                                                                      | Arguments                                                                                         | Description |
176 | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
177 | `` `ASSERT_PULSE``    | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`)              | Assert that signal is an active-high pulse with pulse length of 1 clock cycle                     |
178 | `` `ASSERT_IF``       | `__name`, `__prop`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`) | Assert that a property is true only when an enable signal is set                                  |
179 | `` `ASSERT_KNOWN_IF`` | `__name`, `__sig`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`)  | Assert that signal has a known value (each bit is either '0' or '1') after reset if enable is set |
180 - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*
